āya: [Ā+i+a]  CL=7 (1) Revenue. Profit. Improvement or growth. Income. (2) The prosperity or development of wealth (sampatti) or the prosperity of merits. (3) Ease or comfort (sukha). (4) The power (ādhana) that facilitates the accomplishment of meritorious deeds, leading to comfort or ease (sukha). (5) Coming or approaching. (6) A cause. (7) A place of arising. (A) The place where sāsava dhammas (defilements like disgust, arising from hair, etc.) originate. (B) A place of rising or happening prosperity or wealth. (8) The mental states (citta and cetasika dhammas) that arise at the body door, referred to as āya. (9) (A) A noble cause such as paying proper attention (yonisomanasikāra), etc. (B) The intentional focus that serves as a cause for the arising of merit or demerit. (10) The positive result or fruit of meritorious actions. (11) The pain or suffering (dukkha) that arose from the samudaya lobha. (12) The āyapaccaya ((gram) āya suffix; used to form denominative verbs). (13) The dice called āya (there are 24 kinds of dice such as mālika, sāvaṭṭa, etc.,).
